1. Flow Level Switch: A device that detects the flow rate or level of a fluid in a pipe or tank. It can be used to trigger alarms or control valves based on the measured flow or level.
2. Thermal Electronic: A temperature sensor that uses a thermistor or RTD (Resistance Temperature Detector) to measure temperature. It can be used to monitor the temperature of a fluid or process and trigger alarms or control valves based on the measured temperature.
3. Panel Insert or Case: The enclosure that houses the flow level switch, thermal electronic, and other components. It is typically made of metal or plastic and is designed to protect the components from damage and environmental factors.
4. Relays: Electrical switches that are controlled by an electromagnetic coil. They can be used to switch power to other components or to provide a signal to a control system.
5. Sensing RTDs (Active and Reference): Temperature sensors that use a resistance temperature detector (RTD) to measure temperature. The active RTD is used to measure the temperature of the process fluid, while the reference RTD is used to compensate for changes in ambient temperature.
6. Heater Element: A device that uses electrical resistance to generate heat. It can be used to maintain a minimum temperature in a process or to provide a heat source for a reaction.
7. Digital Display: A device that shows the measured flow rate, level, or temperature on a digital display. It can be used to provide a visual indication of the process status or to allow operators to enter commands or adjust settings.
8. Microprocessor: A computer that controls the operation of the flow level switch and thermal electronic. It can be used to perform calculations, make decisions, and communicate with other devices.
9. Timers: Devices that measure time intervals. They can be used to trigger alarms or control valves based on elapsed time.
10. Push Button Controls: Devices that allow operators to manually control the flow level switch and thermal electronic. They can be used to start or stop the device, adjust settings, or trigger alarms.
